Description: Free national membership for landscape architecture students, with peer and professional connections, student programs, and a path to Associate membership.
Search tool for finding accredited bachelor's and master's programs and the ASLA student chapters at each school.
Introductory guide to the profession: what landscape architects do, the skills needed, choosing a school, and the route to licensure.
Annual juried awards recognizing outstanding student work in design, planning, communications, research, community service, and collaboration.

Description: Annual student-run landscape architecture conference hosted by a different accredited program each year, with lectures, tours, and networking.
Timing / Deadline: Annual; host school rotates (Ohio State in 2026)

Description: ASLA's annual national conference, with student and EP programming, education sessions, networking, and in-person LARE prep workshops.
Timing / Deadline: Annual; typically September, early-bird rates end in June

National committee of Associate members advising ASLA on emerging professional programs; its chair is the voting Associate Representative to the Board.
Timing / Deadline: Two-year terms; nominations each summer via chapter presidents

Description: National committee of student members advising ASLA on student programs; its chair is the voting Student Representative on the Board of Trustees.
Timing / Deadline: Two-year terms; nominations reviewed in August

Description: Many ASLA chapters have EP chairs or committees running local networking, LARE study support, and early-career events.
Annual design competition for emerging professionals, run by the Associate Advisory Committee, with a site tied to the ASLA Conference host city.
Timing / Deadline: Annual; opens spring, entries due mid-July

Description: Annual ASLA honor for one early-career landscape architect showing exceptional leadership and contributions to the profession, community, or firm.
ASLA's job board for landscape architecture positions, with resume, cover letter, interview, and career coaching tools.
Overview of the U.S. licensure path: accredited degree, supervised experience, passing the L.A.R.E., and applying through a state board.
ASLA's L.A.R.E. prep resources: the annual LARE Prep Week, on-demand workshops for all four sections, and conference workshops.

Resource: Women of Color Licensure Advancement Program
Description: ASLA Fund program giving women of color support toward L.A.R.E. fees, exam prep courses, and mentorship from a licensed landscape architect.

Description: Annual scholarships for students with unmet financial need, aimed at increasing participation from underrepresented groups.
Timing / Deadline: Annual; applied for through LAF's scholarship cycle

Practice management courses on the business skills school rarely teaches; many are free for Associates and discounted for students.
Professional Practice Network focused on leadership growth, workplace inclusion, and mentorship across career stages.
More than $150,000 a year across 15+ named scholarships for undergraduate and graduate students in the U.S. and Canada.
LAF's top student honor: universities nominate students, and national winners receive $25,000 (graduate) or $15,000 (undergraduate).
Timing / Deadline: Faculty nominations due February 15; packets due March 15; announced May

Description: Multi-year program for BIPOC students with a $10,000 annual scholarship, a paid summer internship, and one-on-one and peer mentoring.
Timing / Deadline: Applications open each spring; due mid-May

Verified record of education, experience, exam results, and licenses; it is the application for the L.A.R.E. and is sent to licensing boards.

Resource: Your Path to Licensure Webinars & University Talks
Description: Free licensure webinars for students and emerging professionals, plus virtual talks for university professional practice courses.
Timing / Deadline: Through the year; intro webinar each spring and fall

Registration, scheduling, and cancellation deadlines for each exam window; candidates can take up to four sections in one window.

Description: CLARB exam and Record fees, transmittal processing times, and fee policies.
Downloadable guide to exam sections, question types, testing rules, and reference materials; required reading for every candidate.
Official guide to the exam's structure, policies, and the candidate agreement every test-taker accepts.

Fifty-question practice tests built from retired exam questions, with three attempts per section and instant explanations.

How to request testing accommodations, plus comfort aids already approved for use during the exam.
Programs that help pay exam and licensure costs, including Exam Success Grants, reimbursement grants, GI Bill benefits, and Canadian support.

Juried awards for outstanding student research or design work from CELA member schools; winners get full CELA conference registration.
Endowed award for Black, Indigenous, and students of color nominated by their CELA member program, with a $2,000 scholarship.

A graduate student serves on CELA's executive committee as Student Director, with a Director-Elect who takes over next.

List of Canada's LAAC-accredited BLA and MLA programs, which LAAB also recognizes.
CSLA's body that accredits Canadian first professional BLA and MLA programs on a regular review cycle.
Free CSLA membership for students, gained by joining a provincial or territorial component association.
Low-cost membership for associates and interns working toward full membership in a component association.
National awards for the best student work from Canada's accredited programs, in Thesis/Practicum and Studio Project categories.

National recognition for landscape architects early in their careers who show promise and contribute to the profession.
Directory of CSLA's provincial and territorial associations, which handle internship recognition, membership, and registration.

National and regional scholarships for landscape architecture students in Canada, including Indigenous scholarships.
